sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yathā vayaṃ pare rājan yuddhāya samavasthitāḥ yāvac cāsīd balaṃ śiṣṭaṃ saṃgrāme tan nibodha me
english: Saṃjaya said: How we and the foe were arrayed for battle, O king, and what strength yet remained to us in the fray — learn that from me.

sanskrit: ekādaśa sahasrāṇi rathānāṃ bharatarṣabha daśa dantisahasrāṇi sapta caiva śatāni ca
english: Eleven thousand chariots, O bull of the Bhāratas, and ten thousand and seven hundred elephants.

sanskrit: pūrṇe śatasahasre dve hayānāṃ bharatarṣabha narakoṭyas tathā tisro balam etat tavābhavat
english: Two full hundred thousand horses, O bull of the Bhāratas, and three crores of foot-soldiers — such was the force that remained to you.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ ṣaṭsahasrāṇi ṣaṭsahasrāś ca kuñjarāḥ daśa cāśvasahasrāṇi pattikoṭī ca bhārata
english: Six thousand chariots, six thousand elephants, ten thousand horses, and one crore of foot, O Bhārata —

sanskrit: etad balaṃ pāṇḍavānām abhavac cheṣam āhave eta eva samājagmur yuddhāya bharatarṣabha
english: this was the strength of the Pāṇḍavas that remained in the battle; these very ones came together for the fight, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: evaṃ vibhajya rājendra madrarājamate sthitāḥ pāṇḍavān pratyudīyāma jayagṛddhāḥ pramanyavaḥ
english: Having thus divided our forces, O lord of kings, and standing by the counsel of the king of the Madras, we advanced against the Pāṇḍavas, greedy for victory and filled with wrath.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ śūrāḥ samare jitakāśinaḥ upayātā naravyāghrāḥ pāñcālāś ca yaśasvinaḥ
english: In like manner the valiant Pāṇḍavas, those tigers among men wearing the look of victors in battle, advanced, and with them the glorious Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: evam ete balaughena parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ upayātā naravyāghrāḥ pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ prati prabho
english: Thus these tigers among men, each seeking the other's death, advanced with their flood of forces toward the eastern twilight, O lord.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca nighnatām itaretaram
english: Then began a battle of dreadful aspect and terrifying, as your men and the enemy slew one another.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ kurūṇāṃ bhayavardhanam sṛñjayaiḥ saha rājendra ghoraṃ devāsuropamam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then began a battle that swelled the terror of the Kurus, fought against the Sṛñjayas, O lord of kings — a dreadful one, like that of the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: narā rathā gajaughāś ca sādinaś ca sahasraśaḥ vājinaś ca parākrāntāḥ samājagmuḥ parasparam
english: Men, chariots, droves of elephants, horsemen by the thousands, and valiant steeds came together against one another.

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ bhīmarūpāṇāṃ dravatāṃ nisvano mahān aśrūyata yathā kāle jaladānāṃ nabhastale
english: The great roar of the charging elephants of dreadful form was heard, like that of rain-clouds in the sky at the appointed season.

sanskrit: nāgair abhyāhatāḥ ke cit sarathā rathino 'patan vyadravanta raṇe vīrā drāvyamāṇā madotkaṭaiḥ
english: Struck by the elephants, some chariot-warriors fell together with their cars, and heroes fled in the battle, driven before the rut-maddened beasts.

sanskrit: hayaughān pādarakṣāṃś ca rathinas tatra śikṣitāḥ śaraiḥ saṃpreṣayām āsuḥ paralokāya bhārata
english: There the trained chariot-warriors with their arrows dispatched whole troops of horses and the foot-guards to the other world, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sādinaḥ śikṣitā rājan parivārya mahārathān vicaranto raṇe 'bhyaghnan prāsaśaktyṛṣṭibhis tathā
english: The skilled horsemen, O king, surrounding the great chariot-warriors and ranging through the battle, struck them with lances, spears, and double-edged swords.

sanskrit: dhanvinaḥ puruṣāḥ ke cit saṃnivārya mahārathān ekaṃ bahava āsādya preṣayeyur yamakṣayam
english: Certain bowmen, beating back the great chariot-warriors, many of them closing upon a single foe, would send him to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: nāgaṃ rathavarāṃś cānye parivārya mahārathāḥ sottarāyudhinaṃ jaghnur dravamāṇā mahāravam
english: Other great chariot-warriors, surrounding an elephant with its fighters above, slew it as it charged with a mighty trumpeting.

sanskrit: tathā ca rathinaṃ kruddhaṃ vikirantaṃ śarān bahūn nāgā jaghnur mahārāja parivārya samantataḥ
english: And likewise the elephants, O great king, encircling on every side an enraged chariot-warrior who scattered many shafts, slew him.

sanskrit: nāgo nāgam abhidrutya rathī ca rathinaṃ raṇe śaktitomaranārācair nijaghnus tatra tatra ha
english: Elephant rushing against elephant, and chariot-warrior against chariot-warrior in the battle, they slew one another here and there with darts, javelins, and iron shafts.

sanskrit: pādātān avamṛdnanto rathavāraṇavājinaḥ raṇamadhye vyadṛśyanta kurvanto mahad ākulam
english: Chariots, elephants, and horses were seen in the midst of the battle, trampling down the foot-soldiers and wreaking great confusion.

sanskrit: hayāś ca paryadhāvanta cāmarair upaśobhitāḥ haṃsā himavataḥ prasthe pibanta iva medinīm
english: The horses, adorned with yak-tail whisks, raced about as though they were swans drinking up the earth on a tableland of the Himālaya.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu vājināṃ bhūmiḥ khuraiś citrā viśāṃ pate aśobhata yathā nārī karajakṣatavikṣatā
english: The ground, dappled by the hooves of those steeds, O lord of peoples, gleamed like a woman scored and marked by the scratches of nails.

sanskrit: vājināṃ khuraśabdena rathanemisvanena ca pattīnāṃ cāpi śabdena nāgānāṃ bṛṃhitena ca
english: With the clatter of the horses' hooves, the rumble of the chariot-wheels, the shouting of the foot-soldiers, and the trumpeting of the elephants —

sanskrit: vāditrāṇāṃ ca ghoṣeṇa śaṅkhānāṃ nisvanena ca abhavan nāditā bhūmir nirghātair iva bhārata
english: with the din of the war-drums and the blare of the conches, the earth was made to resound as if by thunderclaps, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhanuṣāṃ kūjamānānāṃ nistriṃśānāṃ ca dīpyatām kavacānāṃ prabhābhiś ca na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: From the twanging of the bows, the flashing of the swords, and the glare of the armor, nothing at all could be discerned.

sanskrit: bahavo bāhavaś chinnā nāgarājakaropamāḥ udveṣṭante viveṣṭante vegaṃ kurvanti dāruṇam
english: Many severed arms, like the trunks of lordly elephants, writhed and twisted and jerked with a dreadful violence.

sanskrit: śirasāṃ ca mahārāja patatāṃ vasudhātale cyutānām iva tālebhyaḥ phalānāṃ śrūyate svanaḥ
english: And the sound of the heads falling to the earth, O great king, was heard like that of fruits dropping from palm-trees.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ patitair bhāti rudhirārdrair vasuṃdharā tapanīyanibhaiḥ kāle nalinair iva bhārata
english: With the fallen heads, drenched in blood and gleaming like burnished gold, the earth shone as though strewn with lotuses in their season, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: udvṛttanayanais tais tu gatasattvaiḥ suvikṣataiḥ vyabhrājata mahārāja puṇḍarīkair ivāvṛtā
english: With those heads, their eyes upturned, their life gone, sorely gashed, the earth blazed forth, O great king, as if covered with white lotuses.

sanskrit: bāhubhiś candanādigdhaiḥ sakeyūrair mahādhanaiḥ patitair bhāti rājendra mahī śakradhvajair iva
english: With the arms anointed with sandal-paste, decked with armlets and rich ornaments, fallen there, the earth shone, O lord of kings, as though set with the banners of Indra.

sanskrit: ūrubhiś ca narendrāṇāṃ vinikṛttair mahāhave hastihastopamair anyaiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ tad raṇāṅgaṇam
english: And with the thighs of the lords of men, hewn off in that great battle, and with others like the trunks of elephants, that battlefield was strewn over.

sanskrit: kabandhaśatasaṃkīrṇaṃ chatracāmaraśobhitam senāvanaṃ tac chuśubhe vanaṃ puṣpācitaṃ yathā
english: Thronged with hundreds of headless trunks, adorned with parasols and whisks, that forest of armies shone like a wood heaped with blossoms.

sanskrit: tatra yodhā mahārāja vicaranto hy abhītavat dṛśyante rudhirāktāṅgāḥ puṣpitā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: There the warriors, O great king, ranging about fearlessly, their limbs smeared with blood, were seen like kiṃśuka trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: mātaṅgāś cāpy adṛśyanta śaratomarapīḍitāḥ patantas tatra tatraiva chinnābhrasadṛśā raṇe
english: The elephants too were seen, tormented by arrows and javelins, falling here and there in the battle like sundered clouds.

sanskrit: gajānīkaṃ mahārāja vadhyamānaṃ mahātmabhiḥ vyadīryata diśaḥ sarvā vātanunnā ghanā iva
english: The host of elephants, O great king, slaughtered by the great-souled warriors, broke and scattered to every quarter like clouds driven by the wind.

sanskrit: te gajā ghanasaṃkāśāḥ petur urvyāṃ samantataḥ vajrarugṇā iva babhuḥ parvatā yugasaṃkṣaye
english: Those elephants, resembling clouds, fell upon the earth on every side, looking like mountains shattered by the thunderbolt at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: hayānāṃ sādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ patitānāṃ mahītale rāśayaḥ saṃpradṛśyante girimātrās tatas tataḥ
english: Heaps of horses fallen upon the ground together with their riders were seen here and there, each great as a hill.

sanskrit: saṃjajñe raṇabhūmau tu paralokavahā nadī śoṇitodā rathāvartā dhvajavṛkṣāsthiśarkarā
english: On the field of battle there arose a river bearing men to the other world: its water was blood, its whirlpools were chariots, its trees were banners, its gravel was bones.

sanskrit: bhujanakrā dhanuḥsrotā hastiśailā hayopalā medomajjākardaminī chatrahaṃsā gadoḍupā
english: Its crocodiles were arms, its current was bows, its rocks were elephants, its pebbles were horses; its mire was marrow and fat, its swans were parasols, its rafts were maces.

sanskrit: kavacoṣṇīṣasaṃchannā patākāruciradrumā cakracakrāvalījuṣṭā triveṇūdaṇḍakāvṛtā
english: It was covered over with armor and turbans, its lovely trees were the banners, it teemed with rings of chariot-wheels, and it was strewn with the three-fold poles and shafts of the cars.

sanskrit: śūrāṇāṃ harṣajananī bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhinī prāvartata nadī raudrā kurusṛñjayasaṃkulā
english: Gladdening to the brave and swelling the terror of cowards, that fearsome river flowed on, crowded with Kurus and Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: tāṃ nadīṃ pitṛlokāya vahantīm atibhairavām terur vāhananaubhis te śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ
english: That most terrible river, bearing men to the realm of the fathers, those heroes with arms like iron bars crossed by the boats of their mounts.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yuddhe nirmaryāde viśāṃ pate caturaṅgakṣaye ghore pūrvaṃ devāsuropame
english: As that battle without bounds raged on, O lord of peoples, in the dreadful destruction of the four arms of the host, like the war of old between the gods and the asuras —

sanskrit: akrośan bāndhavān anye tatra tatra paraṃtapa krośadbhir bāndhavaiś cānye bhayārtā na nivartire
english: some there cried out to their kinsmen here and there, O scorcher of foes, while others, called to by their kinsmen, were so stricken with fear that they did not turn back.

sanskrit: nirmaryāde tathā yuddhe vartamāne bhayānake arjuno bhīmasenaś ca mohayāṃ cakratuḥ parān
english: As that terrible battle without bounds raged on, Arjuna and Bhīmasena threw the enemy into bewilderment.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā mahatī senā tava janādhipa amuhyat tatra tatraiva yoṣin madavaśād iva
english: That great host of yours, being slaughtered, O lord of men, swooned away here and there, like a woman overcome by drink.

sanskrit: mohayitvā ca tāṃ senāṃ bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau dadhmatur vārijau tatra siṃhanādaṃ ca nedatuḥ
english: And having confounded that army, Bhīmasena and Dhanaṃjaya blew their conches there and roared their lion-roars.

sanskrit: śrutvaiva tu mahāśabdaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau dharmarājaṃ puraskṛtya madrarājam abhidrutau
english: No sooner had they heard that mighty sound than Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, placing the King of Righteousness at their head, rushed upon the king of the Madras.

sanskrit: tatrāścaryam apaśyāma ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate śalyena saṃgatāḥ śūrā yad ayudhyanta bhāgaśaḥ
english: There we beheld a wonder of dreadful aspect, O lord of peoples — how those heroes, met with Śalya, fought him each in his own division.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau sarabhasau kṛtāstrau yuddhadurmadau abhyayātāṃ tvarāyuktau jigīṣantau balaṃ tava
english: The two sons of Mādrī, impetuous, accomplished in arms, drunk with the lust of war, advanced in haste, eager to overcome your force.

sanskrit: tato nyavartata balaṃ tāvakaṃ bharatarṣabha śaraiḥ praṇunnaṃ bahudhā pāṇḍavair jitakāśibhiḥ
english: Then your army turned back, O bull of the Bhāratas, driven in many directions by the arrows of the Pāṇḍavas who wore the look of victors.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā camūḥ sā tu putrāṇāṃ prekṣatāṃ tava bheje diśo mahārāja praṇunnā dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ hāhākāro mahāñ jajñe yodhānāṃ tava bhārata
english: That host, cut down while your sons looked on, fled to every quarter, O great king, driven before the stout bowmen; and a great cry of woe arose among your warriors, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vāg āsīd drāvitānāṃ mahātmanām kṣatriyāṇāṃ tadānyonyaṃ saṃyuge jayam icchatām ādravann eva bhagnās te pāṇḍavais tava sainikāḥ
english: "Stand, stand!" was the cry of the great-souled kṣatriyas who were put to flight, each desiring victory over the other in the fray; yet your soldiers, broken by the Pāṇḍavas, only fled the faster.

sanskrit: tyaktvā yuddhe priyān putrān bhrātṝn atha pitāmahān mātulān bhāgineyāṃś ca tathā saṃbandhibāndhavān
english: Abandoning in the battle their dear sons, brothers, grandsires, maternal uncles, sisters' sons, and kinsmen and friends as well,

sanskrit: hayān dvipāṃs tvarayanto yodhā jagmuḥ samantataḥ ātmatrāṇakṛtotsāhās tāvakā bharatarṣabha
english: your warriors fled in every direction, urging on their horses and elephants, bent only upon the saving of their own lives, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tat prabhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā madrarājaḥ pratāpavān uvāca sārathiṃ tūrṇaṃ codayāśvān mahājavān
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing that force shattered, the valorous king of the Madras swiftly said to his charioteer: "Urge on the horses of great speed!

sanskrit: eṣa tiṣṭhati vai rājā pāṇḍuputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ chatreṇa dhriyamāṇena pāṇḍureṇa virājatā
english: Yonder stands the king Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pāṇḍu, resplendent beneath a white parasol held aloft over him.

sanskrit: atra māṃ prāpaya kṣipraṃ paśya me sārathe balam na samarthā hi me pārthāḥ sthātum adya puro yudhi
english: Bear me thither at once; behold my strength, O charioteer — the sons of Pṛthā are not able to stand before me in battle this day."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ prāyān madrarājasya sārathiḥ yatra rājā satyasaṃdho dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Thus addressed, the charioteer of the king of the Madras set forth toward where the truthful King of Righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, stood.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ ca sahasā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam dadhāraiko raṇe śalyo velevoddhṛtam arṇavam
english: And the great host of the Pāṇḍavas rushing suddenly on, Śalya alone in the battle held back, as a shore holds back the heaving ocean.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ balaughas tu śalyam āsādya māriṣa vyatiṣṭhata tadā yuddhe sindhor vega ivācalam
english: The flood of the Pāṇḍava force, coming upon Śalya, O honored sir, was stayed in the battle, like the current of the Indus against a mountain.

sanskrit: madrarājaṃ tu samare dṛṣṭvā yuddhāya viṣṭhitam kuravaḥ saṃnyavartanta mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Beholding the king of the Madras stationed for battle in the fray, the Kurus rallied back, making of death itself their turning-point.

sanskrit: teṣu rājan nivṛtteṣu vyūḍhānīkeṣu bhāgaśaḥ prāvartata mahāraudraḥ saṃgrāmaḥ śoṇitodakaḥ samārchac citrasenena nakulo yuddhadurmadaḥ
english: When they had rallied, O king, their ranks arrayed in their several divisions, a most dreadful combat began, its water blood; and Nakula, drunk with the frenzy of war, closed with Citrasena.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya citrakārmukadhāriṇau meghāv iva yathodvṛttau dakṣiṇottaravarṣiṇau
english: Those two, closing upon each other, each bearing a gleaming bow, were like two upreared clouds pouring rain from the south and the north.

sanskrit: śaratoyaiḥ siṣicatus tau parasparam āhave nāntaraṃ tatra paśyāmi pāṇḍavasyetarasya vā
english: With showers of arrows for their rain they drenched each other in the battle; I could mark no difference there between the Pāṇḍava and the other.

sanskrit: ubhau kṛtāstrau balinau rathacaryāviśāradau parasparavadhe yattau chidrānveṣaṇatatparau
english: Both were accomplished in arms, both mighty, both skilled in the maneuvering of chariots, both intent upon slaying the other and eager to spy out his opening.

sanskrit: citrasenas tu bhallena pītena niśitena ca nakulasya mahārāja muṣṭideśe 'cchinad dhanuḥ
english: But Citrasena, with a yellow, whetted, broad-headed shaft, severed Nakula's bow, O great king, at the place of the grip.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ tribhiḥ śarair asaṃbhrānto lalāṭe vai samarpayat
english: Then, his bow cut away, unflinching Citrasena planted three arrows with golden shafts, sharpened on stone, full upon his brow.

sanskrit: hayāṃś cāsya śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ preṣayām āsa mṛtyave tathā dhvajaṃ sārathiṃ ca tribhis tribhir apātayat
english: And with sharp arrows he sent his horses to their death, and with three shafts each he brought down his banner and his charioteer.

sanskrit: sa śatrubhujanirmuktair lalāṭasthais tribhiḥ śaraiḥ nakulaḥ śuśubhe rājaṃs triśṛṅga iva parvataḥ
english: With those three arrows loosed from the enemy's arm and lodged in his brow, Nakula shone, O king, like a three-peaked mountain.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā virathaḥ khaḍgam ādāya carma ca rathād avātarad vīraḥ śailāgrād iva kesarī
english: His bow cut, his chariot lost, the hero took up sword and shield and leapt down from his car, like a lion from a mountain-peak.

sanskrit: padbhyām āpatatas tasya śaravṛṣṭim avāsṛjat nakulo 'py agrasat tāṃ vai carmaṇā laghuvikramaḥ
english: As he came on afoot, Citrasena loosed a rain of arrows upon him; but Nakula, swift in his prowess, swallowed it up with his shield.

sanskrit: citrasenarathaṃ prāpya citrayodhī jitaśramaḥ āruroha mahābāhuḥ sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Reaching Citrasena's chariot, that wondrous fighter, mighty-armed and unwearied, mounted it as the whole army looked on.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ samukuṭaṃ sunasaṃ svāyatekṣaṇam citrasenaśiraḥ kāyād apāharata pāṇḍavaḥ sa papāta rathopasthād divākarasamaprabhaḥ
english: With its earrings, its diadem, its shapely nose, and its long fine eyes, the Pāṇḍava struck Citrasena's head from his body; and he fell from the floor of the car, radiant as the sun.

sanskrit: citrasenaṃ viśastaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tatra mahārathāḥ sādhuvādasvanāṃś cakruḥ siṃhanādāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: Seeing Citrasena slain there, the great chariot-warriors raised shouts of approval and many a lion-roar.

sanskrit: viśastaṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇaputrau mahārathau suṣeṇaḥ satyasenaś ca muñcantau niśitāñ śarān
english: Seeing their brother slain, the two sons of Karṇa, those great chariot-warriors Suṣeṇa and Satyasena, loosing whetted arrows,

sanskrit: tato 'bhyadhāvatāṃ tūrṇaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ rathināṃ varam jighāṃsantau yathā nāgaṃ vyāghrau rājan mahāvane
english: thereupon rushed swiftly against the Pāṇḍava, that best of chariot-warriors, longing to slay him, as two tigers fall upon an elephant, O king, in a great forest.

sanskrit: tāv abhyadhāvatāṃ tīkṣṇau dvāv apy enaṃ mahāratham śaraughān samyag asyantau jīmūtau salilaṃ yathā
english: Those two fierce ones, both of them, charged that great chariot-warrior, pouring forth floods of arrows aright, as two storm-clouds pour down rain.

sanskrit: sa śaraiḥ sarvato viddhaḥ prahṛṣṭa iva pāṇḍavaḥ anyat kārmukam ādāya ratham āruhya vīryavān atiṣṭhata raṇe vīraḥ kruddharūpa ivāntakaḥ
english: Pierced on every side by their arrows, the Pāṇḍava, as though delighted, took up another bow, and the valiant hero, mounting his chariot, stood in the battle like Death himself in the form of wrath.

sanskrit: tasya tau bhrātarau rājañ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ rathaṃ viśakalīkartuṃ samārabdhau viśāṃ pate
english: The two brothers, O king, with arrows whose joints were well-knit, set about to break his chariot to pieces, O lord of peoples.
